skills.name: Competitor Analysis & Battlecard
skills.description: Takes competitor URLs, release notes, or positioning dumps, compares them against .context/ product specs, and outputs a feature parity matrix, differentiation gaps, and a 1-page Sales/PM battlecard.

skills.name: Modular Framework Runner
skills.description: Executes modular strategic, discovery, or prioritization frameworks from frameworks/ over an idea, backlog, or PRD, and synchronizes results back to .context/.

skills.name: Spec Auditor & Pre-Mortem Critique
skills.description: Audits draft PRDs and User Stories against .context/ single source of truth, flagging scope creep, missing edge cases, unvalidated assumptions, and architectural conflicts.

skills.name: Opportunity Brainstorm
skills.description: Facilitates structured product & feature brainstorming using SCAMPER, How Might We (HMW), 6 Thinking Hats, and Value vs. Effort matrix.

skills.name: Compact Context & Memory Inbox
skills.description: Merges staged .context/.inbox/ patches after human review and compacts bloated .context/*.md files using Anchored Incremental Summarization without losing foundational decisions.

skills.name: MCP Integration Manager
skills.description: Establishes, tests, and manages Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations for external PM tools: Atlassian (Jira & Confluence), GitHub Issues, Figma, Miro, Notion, and Google Stitch across AGY, Claude Code, and Cursor IDEs.

skills.name: UI/UX Design Brief
skills.description: Creates comprehensive UI/UX Design Briefs including design objectives, user context, step-by-step user flows, component specs, WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility guidelines, and Figma handoff criteria.

skills.name: Technical & User Docs
skills.description: Generates dual-purpose technical and end-user documentation. Produces API schemas (OpenAPI format), Mermaid sequence diagrams, architecture specs, and step-by-step end-user manuals.

skills.name: HTML Wireframe & Prototype
skills.description: Generates clickable, interactive UI mockups and prototypes as self-contained HTML files styled with Tailwind CSS, supporting interactive tabs, modals, forms, and responsive device views.

skills.name: PRD Generator
skills.description: Generates comprehensive Product Requirements Documents (PRDs) across 3 modes: Lean (Startup/MVP), Standard Agile (Growth/Mid-size), and Enterprise (Compliance/Scale).

skills.name: Outcome Roadmap Generator
skills.description: Transforms BACKLOG.md, .context/discovery.md, and prioritization scores into a stakeholder-ready Now / Next / Later or Quarterly OKR Outcome Roadmap.

skills.name: Stakeholder Update & Release Notes
skills.description: Synthesizes recent changes in BACKLOG.md, .context/decisions.md, and docs/ into tailored communications: Executive Weekly Digest, Engineering/Cross-Functional Update, or Customer-Facing Release Notes.

skills.name: INVEST User Stories
skills.description: Generates user stories adhering to INVEST criteria, Concur format (As a/I want/So that), Gherkin Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria, Fibonacci story points, and Definition of Done across Lean, Standard Agile, and Enterprise modes.

skills.name: Metrics & Experiment Plan
skills.description: Defines feature success metrics (North Star, Primary, Guardrail), event tracking taxonomy (events + properties), and A/B test or rollout hypotheses before engineering begins building.

skills.name: Post-Launch Retrospective
skills.description: Evaluates post-launch performance data against the PRD's original success metrics, logs whether the bet succeeded/failed/iterated, and writes lessons learned back to .context/decisions.md.

skills.name: PM Command Center GUI
skills.description: Launches the PM Command Center visual web application (GUI) locally on port 3000 and automatically opens it in your default web browser.

skills.name: Context Ingestion Router
skills.description: Ingests raw unstructured inputs (meeting notes, customer interview transcripts, Slack dumps, existing PRDs, codebase READMEs, or MCP pages) and routes structured updates into .context/ product knowledge files.

skills.name: GTM Launch Plan
skills.description: Generates a tiered launch plan (Tier 1 Major, Tier 2 Standard, Tier 3 Silent) from a PRD, including positioning messaging, internal enablement FAQs, rollout checklists, and rollback triggers.

skills.name: Meeting Prep & Defense Brief
skills.description: Prepares a 1-page briefing doc before a tough stakeholder review, board meeting, or customer call, pulling past decisions, anticipated objections, trade-off options, and talking points.

skills.name: User Interview Script & Guide
skills.description: Generates non-leading Mom Test interview guides, screener questions, and assumption probes tailored to a specific target persona and hypothesis before user discovery sessions.

skills.name: Framework Dispatcher
skills.description: Diagnoses PM bottlenecks, uncertainty, or prioritization challenges, recommends the optimal framework & skill with a lightweight alternative and anti-pattern warning, and guides execution.

skills.name: Story Refinement & SPIDR
skills.description: Grooms and refines existing user stories. Detects ambiguity, splits large stories using the SPIDR framework, adds missing Gherkin edge cases, and calculates a Grooming Readiness Score (0-100%).

skills.name: Sync Delivery Backlog (Jira & GitHub)
skills.description: Pushes and pulls epics, user stories, acceptance criteria, and sprint status between local PM artifacts and issue trackers (Jira or GitHub Issues) via MCP.

skills.name: Sync Docs & Design (Confluence, Notion, Figma, Miro)
skills.description: Synchronizes PRDs, documentation, discovery maps, and design briefs with knowledge bases (Confluence, Notion) and visual collaboration tools (Figma, Miro) via MCP.

skills.name: Linear Issues & Cycles Sync
skills.description: Bi-directionally syncs Linear issues, cycles, projects, and triage queues via Model Context Protocol (MCP). Imports Linear issues into BACKLOG.md and .context/discovery.md, or exports INVEST user stories to Linear.

skills.name: Customer Feedback Triage
skills.description: Batch-processes raw customer feedback, support tickets, NPS verbatims, or sales call notes, clustering them by frequency and severity, and mapping them to opportunities in .context/discovery.md.

skills.name: Idea & Hypothesis Validator
skills.description: Validates product ideas, feature concepts, and business hypotheses using Strategyzer 4-Risk Analysis, Osterwalder's 44-Experiment Selector, The Mom Test customer interview framework, TAM/SAM/SOM market sizing, and Pre-mortem risk identification.

frameworks.name: AARRR Pirate Metrics & Growth Loops
frameworks.description: To diagnose exactly where the user conversion leaks occur, fix the "leaky bucket" before spending money on acquisition, and architect compounding, product-led distribution loops.
problem_signatures: User acquisition is growing but revenue or retention is flatlining (leaky bucket syndrome)
Growth model relies entirely on paid linear ads rather than compounding self-reinforcing product loops
Team cannot pinpoint the exact drop-off step in the user onboarding funnel
when_not_to_use: Early 0-to-1 pre-product-market fit where retention has not stabilized for even 10 users
Pure B2B high-touch enterprise sales where buying cycles are 9 months of RFP committee negotiations

frameworks.name: Assumption Mapping & Riskiest Assumption Test (RAT)
frameworks.description: To eliminate leap-of-faith failures and prevent engineering teams from spending months building products or features that nobody wants, cannot be monetized, or hit insurmountable technical roadblocks.
problem_signatures: Team is preparing to build a major feature based on unverified team opinions rather than customer evidence
Unclear which risk (desirability, feasibility, viability, usability) could kill the product first
Over-investing in high-fidelity prototypes when a simple landing page or customer inquiry test would suffice
when_not_to_use: Standard maintenance tasks, refactoring, or compliance mandates with known solutions and zero user uncertainty
Optimizing high-traffic checkout funnels where quantitative multivariate A/B testing is already active

frameworks.name: Osterwalder 44-Experiment Selector & Sequencing Engine
frameworks.description: To deterministically match any product idea or Zone 1 risky assumption against Osterwalder & Bland's 44 experiments by **Risk Type (`D/V/F/U`)**, **Market (`B2B/B2C`)**, **Cost/Time**, and **Evidence Strength**, outputting the **Top 2–3 Matched Experiments** and a **2-Step Sequence** without context bloat.
problem_signatures: Team has identified a risky assumption (RAT) but defaults to generic customer interviews or building a full MVP instead of matching the optimal experiment
PM manually flips through 'Testing Business Ideas' (Bland & Osterwalder) trying to cross-reference 44 experiments by risk type, B2B/B2C context, cost, time, and evidence strength
Testing Viability (willingness to pay) with opinion surveys ('What people say') instead of behavioral skin-in-the-game ('What people do')
when_not_to_use: Zero-uncertainty bug fixes, regulatory compliance mandates, or internal infrastructural refactoring
When the team has not yet articulated the underlying risky assumption (run assumption-mapping first)

frameworks.name: Jobs-to-be-Done (JTBD) & The Mom Test
frameworks.description: To uncover genuine customer demand by systematically filtering out false validation, identifying real customer struggle, and structuring value propositions around the forces that drive adoption.
problem_signatures: Customers give polite compliments in interviews but never buy, activate, or retain
Feature specifications anchor on opinions and generic hypothetical promises
Team cannot articulate the functional, emotional, and social struggle driving adoption
when_not_to_use: Optimizing high-traffic checkout funnels where A/B testing statistical data is available
Internal infrastructural refactoring with no user-facing behavioral component

frameworks.name: Opportunity Solution Tree (OST)
frameworks.description: To break the "feature factory" anti-pattern by ensuring teams explore the problem space thoroughly, evaluate multiple competing solutions for each customer pain point, and test assumptions before committing engineering resources.
problem_signatures: Team operates as a feature factory shipping random stakeholder solution requests
Features lack direct traceability to measurable business outcomes
Engineers jump to building the first idea without considering alternative solutions
when_not_to_use: Immediate production outage triage or critical regulatory compliance deadlines
Teams where executive leadership mandates fixed Gantt-chart feature lists

frameworks.name: GIST Planning (Goals, Ideas, Step-projects, Tasks)
frameworks.description: To drastically reduce product waste by testing ideas through tiny step-projects before committing full engineering squads to building multi-month feature implementations.
problem_signatures: Annual or quarterly roadmaps become obsolete within weeks of leadership sign-off
Teams commit to multi-month solutions before validating whether the core concept works
Disconnect between high-level company OKRs and daily sprint execution tasks
when_not_to_use: Strict contractual or outsourced development with rigid upfront milestone specifications
Hardware or physical manufacturing pipelines where step-projects cannot ship iteratively

frameworks.name: Continuous Kanban & Service Level Expectations (SLE)
frameworks.description: To eliminate sprint-end crunch and rollover anxiety, stabilize flow predictability, shorten lead time from idea to production, and ensure operational readiness when `operating_model: kanban` is active in `.context/harness-config.yaml`.
problem_signatures: Teams struggle with sprint batching friction and artificial 2-week boundary overhead
Work-in-progress (WIP) bloat causes lead times and cycle times to blow out unpredictably
High-priority production bugs and urgent customer requests constantly disrupt sprint commitments
when_not_to_use: Early 0-to-1 exploratory spikes where workflows have no distinct linear stages
Contract-driven waterfall releases requiring fixed-scope, fixed-date milestone sign-offs

frameworks.name: Pre-Mortem (Tigers, Paper Tigers & Elephants)
frameworks.description: To normalize the voice of dissent, prevent preventable launch disasters, clear away unproductive anxiety over minor edge cases, and confront taboo blockers while there is still time to adjust scope.
problem_signatures: Teams experience catastrophic launch-day surprises that could easily have been anticipated
Engineering and business teams waste excessive energy debating vocal but harmless minor worries
Nobody on the team feels safe speaking up about known fatal architectural or organizational flaws
when_not_to_use: Low-risk, reversible routine bug fixes or internal copy changes
Teams where psychological safety is so damaged that risk identification is weaponized

frameworks.name: Scrum Sprint Delivery & INVEST Execution
frameworks.description: To provide predictable, sustainable, cross-functional engineering throughput with continuous delivery of shippable software increments.
problem_signatures: Sprints fail repeatedly because stories are too large, ambiguous, or unestimated
Engineers build literal ticket text rather than solving the real customer need
Lack of clear Definition of Ready (DoR) causes continuous mid-sprint scope churn
when_not_to_use: Tiny 1-2 person exploratory teams where meeting ceremonies create pure overhead
High-uncertainty innovation spikes where scope cannot be estimated into 2-week commitments

frameworks.name: Shape Up (Basecamp Product Development)
frameworks.description: To eliminate endless scope creep, eliminate backlog grooming debt, and empower autonomous cross-functional teams to deliver complete, polished features within bounded timeboxes.
problem_signatures: Projects drag on indefinitely with continuous sprint rollovers and creeping scope
Engineers receive UI wireframes that are too rigid or PRDs that are too vague
Backlog grooming has degraded into an endless backlog management chore
when_not_to_use: Fixed-scope enterprise contractual deliverables with strict external deadlines
Pure maintenance, continuous firefighting, or infrastructure incident response teams

frameworks.name: User Story Mapping (Jeff Patton)
frameworks.description: To eliminate "flat backlog blindness", ensure teams ship complete, coherent end-to-end user journeys rather than disconnected vertical feature fragments, and establish clear release boundaries based on value increments.
problem_signatures: Backlog is a flat, unprioritized list of tickets with no visibility into the end-to-end customer journey
Teams struggle to carve out a true Walking Skeleton MVP without scope creeping into a monolithic release
Stories are released out of sequence, stranding users in half-finished or broken task flows
when_not_to_use: Pure backend infrastructure migration or algorithmic performance tuning with zero user workflow
Single bug fixes or minor cosmetic copy tweaks that do not touch user journey steps

frameworks.name: ICE & Value vs. Effort Prioritization
frameworks.description: To deliver rapid, transparent prioritization when teams are in early stages, lack large-scale statistical telemetry for RICE, or need to unblock backlog paralysis in under 15 minutes.
problem_signatures: Team lacks quantitative reach and conversion telemetry required to run RICE without guessing
Need a fast, 15-minute consensus scoring method to rank a brainstormed backlog of 15+ ideas
Stakeholders disagree on whether to prioritize quick wins versus long-term strategic investments
when_not_to_use: High-scale mature products with robust funnel analytics where RICE or WSJF provides mathematically superior economic scheduling
Contractually committed enterprise roadmap items where scope is legally mandated

frameworks.name: The Kano Model & Customer Delight
frameworks.description: To construct balanced product releases that satisfy table-stakes baseline requirements, compete effectively on performance, and incorporate distinct delighters while aggressively pruning indifferent bloat.
problem_signatures: MVP scope suffers from feature creep and lacks differentiation from competitors
Unclear distinction between table-stakes basic features and true delighters
Customer feedback surveys show mixed signals on what features to build next
when_not_to_use: Internal architectural refactors or purely operational workflow optimizations
Scenarios where functional and dysfunctional survey data cannot be collected

frameworks.name: MoSCoW & Buy-a-Feature Scope Negotiation
frameworks.description: To establish enforceable release boundaries, protect developers from burnout, and prevent the "everything is high priority" trap during fixed-date enterprise deliveries.
problem_signatures: Stakeholders treat every feature request as an absolute P0 must-have
Release deadlines are fixed by contractual commitments but scope keeps ballooning
Scope cutting meetings devolve into political turf wars without clear budget boundaries
when_not_to_use: Early 0-to-1 exploratory spikes where user problem discovery is still fluid
Teams running small, continuous single-piece flow without batch milestone releases

frameworks.name: Opportunity Scoring (Importance vs. Satisfaction)
frameworks.description: To eliminate the wasteful "feature trap" of improving capabilities that customers already find "good enough", and redirect resources toward high-importance jobs where customers remain acutely dissatisfied.
problem_signatures: Team is over-investing in features where customer satisfaction is already high (over-served market)
Critical customer needs are severely underserved, but ignored because no vocal stakeholder advocates for them
Prioritization relies on subjective HIPPO opinions rather than quantitative customer satisfaction gaps
when_not_to_use: Early 0-to-1 concept phase where customers have never experienced a candidate solution
Internal devops pipelines where customer satisfaction surveys cannot be administered

frameworks.name: RICE Scoring Matrix
frameworks.description: To eliminate cognitive bias, loud-stakeholder lobbying, and "pet project" syndrome by anchoring prioritization to empirical reach, measurable business impact, defensible confidence, and engineering effort.
problem_signatures: Backlog is prioritized by who speaks the loudest or highest-paid person's opinion (HiPPO)
Low-impact pet projects consistently displace high-reach core features
Teams lack an objective numerical basis to resolve stakeholder feature debates
when_not_to_use: Early 0-to-1 discovery where Reach and Impact numbers are completely speculative
Hard-deadline regulatory or compliance mandates that must be built regardless of reach

frameworks.name: Weighted Shortest Job First (WSJF) & Cost of Delay
frameworks.description: To maximize economic flow by scheduling high-value, time-critical, risk-reducing features that can be delivered quickly, preventing the common failure mode of tying up engineering squads on monolithic, slow-moving projects.
problem_signatures: Slow-moving massive initiatives block fast, high-impact tactical releases
Time-sensitive market opportunities or regulatory deadlines missed due to poor sequencing
Engineering lacks economic rationale for slicing large epics into high-value chunks
when_not_to_use: Early-stage startups with fluid roadmaps where time-to-learn dominates cost-of-delay
Backlogs where job sizing cannot be reliably estimated in story points

frameworks.name: North Star Metric & Input Metric Tree
frameworks.description: To establish a clear causal equation between day-to-day feature development and overall company success, ensuring squads optimize actionable leading indicators without gaming the system.
problem_signatures: Team is optimizing fragmented vanity metrics that do not roll up to sustainable customer value
Different squads or engineers pull in opposing directions without a unified equation of growth
Leadership tracks lagging revenue numbers without actionable leading input metrics for product teams
when_not_to_use: Early customer discovery phase before any initial product value loop or prototype exists
Ad-hoc consulting or custom bespoke software projects with zero recurring usage loops

frameworks.name: Van Westendorp & Packaging/Tiering Matrix
frameworks.description: To establish data-backed pricing boundaries, eliminate monetization guesswork, and package features into clear, high-converting tier boundaries.
problem_signatures: Pricing strategy is based on internal team guesswork rather than empirical customer willingness-to-pay
Feature tiering is confusing and customers resist upgrading between Free, Pro, and Enterprise
Team packages 'killer' core value features into lower tiers, starving higher tiers of upgrade incentives
when_not_to_use: Pure open-source software with zero commercial, monetization, or paid tier ambitions
Early 0-to-1 discovery where customers haven't validated the core value proposition

frameworks.name: Product Positioning (April Dunford)
frameworks.description: To eliminate positioning confusion, elevate differentiation above incumbent competitors, and guide GTM launch messaging, sales battlecards, and PRD scope.
problem_signatures: Prospects and customers say 'So what?' or misunderstand what the product actually does
Sales team struggles to close deals without extensive discounting or custom development
The product competes head-on against entrenched incumbents in the wrong market category
when_not_to_use: Internal platform tools with zero external customer or market positioning considerations
Routine patch releases or minor bug fix updates

frameworks.name: 7 Powers (Hamilton Helmer) Moat Analysis
frameworks.description: To force product managers to distinguish between temporary "features" (easily copied commodities) and structural "powers" that generate enduring enterprise value.
problem_signatures: Features are easily copied by well-funded incumbents within weeks of launching
The product lacks durable structural defensibility or pricing power as it scales
Team confuses temporary operational excellence or speed with long-term strategic moats
when_not_to_use: Early 0-to-1 exploratory spikes where product-market fit has not yet been demonstrated
Internal developer tooling with no commercial or competitive market dynamics

frameworks.name: Theory of Constraints (ToC) & CRT Mapping
frameworks.description: To pinpoint the operational bottleneck choking product delivery, maximize throughput at that specific point, and align all upstream discovery and downstream execution to eliminate waste.
problem_signatures: Engineering delivery velocity stalls despite adding headcount or running more syncs
Backlog grows exponentially while deployment throughput remains completely flat
Upstream requirements or downstream QA continually starves engineering flow
when_not_to_use: Early 0-to-1 discovery where product-market fit has not been established
Environments with no measurable workflow stages or cycle-time metrics

frameworks.name: Wardley Value Chain Evolution Mapping
frameworks.description: To prevent catastrophic resource misallocation (e.g., custom-building commoditized components) and explicitly identify where a product's true competitive differentiation resides.
problem_signatures: Team debates custom-building infrastructure vs buying SaaS or using cloud utilities
Unclear where durable competitive advantage lies in the technology architecture
Risk of investing heavily in capabilities about to be commoditized by vendors
when_not_to_use: Simple tactical UI bug fixes or single-screen user story refinement
Teams without access to or understanding of overall technology architecture

frameworks.name: Working Backwards (Amazon PR/FAQ)
frameworks.description: To enforce extreme customer-centric clarity, prevent technical solipsism, align cross-functional leaders around the core value proposition, and expose unaddressed trade-offs long before development begins.
problem_signatures: Feature concept is heavily engineering-led or architecture-driven without a clear customer value narrative
Product vision is diffuse and executive stakeholders disagree on the core customer experience being built
Team writes massive 30-page spec documents that bury the real customer problem under implementation minutiae
when_not_to_use: Incremental bug fixing, tech debt reduction, or internal pipeline refactoring
Continuous UI polish sprints where the core value proposition is already proven and unchanged

context_files.title: Product Vision, Personas & OKRs
context_files.description: Core product identity, target user personas, primary value loops, North Star metric, and strategic OKRs.

context_files.title: Strategy, Bottlenecks & Constraints

agents.name: discovery-synthesizer
agents.description: Isolated sub-agent that ingests raw, noisy user interview transcripts, support tickets, or competitor notes and distills structured JTBD/OST insights into .context/.inbox/ without bloating the main conversation window.

agents.name: pm-critic
agents.description: Isolated, read-only adversarial PM reviewer. Audits PRDs, user stories, and strategy docs against .context/ constraints, hunting for unvalidated assumptions, feature-factory output, and scope creep.
